- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.25) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3 consecutive days above 75.0), model tends to overpredict; apply 1–2% downward adjustment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg between -0.1 and +0.1), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 2-day weighted average of recent history to anchor short-term forecast.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply gradual decay (e.g., 10% reduction per day).
